label: Déploiement de la bioénergie avec captage et stockage du carbone (BECCS) à grande échelle

sources: IPCC AR6 SYR Section 5 — BECCS features in models limiting warming to 1.5°C as a negative emissions source; net removal 1–3 GtCO2/yr by 2050
IEA Bioenergy with CCS 2023 — BECCS potential 3–10 GtCO2/yr by 2050 depending on sustainable biomass availability and geological storage
Royal Society Greenhouse Gas Removal Report 2018 — CDR technologies including BECCS are necessary but cannot substitute for emissions reduction at source
IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.12 — BECCS contributes to carbon dioxide removal (CDR) but faces land-use, water and biodiversity constraints

planetary_limits.note: Energy crop monocultures can displace natural ecosystems if poorly governed
Competes for land with food production and ecosystem restoration at large scale
Energy crops require significant irrigation in water-scarce regions

societal_indicators.note: Large-scale energy crop cultivation competes with food production for land; governance critical
Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) production with CCS addresses hard-to-abate aviation sector

interactions.note: Shares CO2 transport and geological storage infrastructure; industrial CCS experience accelerates BECCS deployment
Energy crop expansion must not displace areas designated for ecosystem restoration
BECCS must not drive indirect land-use change that leads to deforestation

methodological_note: BECCS is the technology with the largest uncertainty range in the entire catalogue (0.5–5.0 GtCO2/yr net removal). Median impact of 2 GtCO2/yr net removal calibrated against IPCC AR6 WGIII Ch.12 lower estimates. Very long implementation lag (12 years) reflects need for: (1) shared CCS infrastructure from industrial CCS, (2) sustainable biomass supply chain development, (3) governance framework for energy crop certification. Optimistic scenario assumes miscanthus and switchgrass on degraded/marginal land only, avoiding food/biodiversity competition. Forest delta shows slight degradation (-1.3 pp at 2074) due to energy crop land use. Biomass resource delta shows increase (+3.0 Gt/yr) as energy crop demand grows. Projection baseline: SSP2-4.5.
